# At a glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Format | Standard (Reality Fracture, set code `fra`, plus Standard mana support) |
| Colors | Black, red, green (Jund) |
| Archetype | Prepared-value aggro; every creature is a reusable spell that feeds prowess and ping payoffs |
| Size | 60 cards, 26 lands, 34 spells |
| Primary win | Upkeep re-preparation: Woodwork Prodigy and Stingerquill Voxmancer re-arm themselves every turn, so free Soul Tether and Vicious Verse copies keep firing prowess and noncreature-cast triggers |
| Secondary win | Codie, Ravenous Codex copies each prepared spell you cast, then turns every creature on the board prepared at once for an alpha-strike turn |
| Land as engine | Hexhaven Dueling Arena turns an attacker prepared for `{2}`, which is another free spell every combat and another round of prowess and ping triggers |

# Overview

Reality Fracture's flagship mechanic is prepared: a creature enters prepared or is re-armed by a trigger, and while it
is prepared you may cast a copy of the spell printed on its back face. Casting that copy unprepares the creature. Most
prepared creatures therefore give you one free spell. This deck is built on the small group that gives you one **every
single turn**.

Two of them are the engine. **Woodwork Prodigy** (`{2}{R/G}`, 3/3 Cat Druid) becomes prepared at the beginning of your
upkeep if it is not already, and its back face is **Soul Tether** (`{2}{R/G}` sorcery: create a Heartwood token, a red
and green artifact with `{T}: Add {R} or {G}`). **Stingerquill Voxmancer** (`{B/R}`, 1/2 Goblin Sorcerer) has the same
upkeep trigger with **Vicious Verse** (`{B/R}` sorcery: deal 1 damage to target opponent) on the back. One grows your
mana every turn for free; the other bleeds the opponent every turn for free.

The rest of the list is built to convert "free spell, every turn" into damage. Noncreature-cast payoffs turn each copy
into extra points: Firebrand Archer and Firespitter Whelp each deal 1 damage to every opponent, Chandra's Emberling
grows, Grim Repriser comes back from the graveyard, and every prowess creature in the deck gets bigger. Because the
copies cost no mana, the engine runs while your lands are spent on creatures.

The front halves matter too. Heartwood Crafter and Konstrari Improviser enter prepared, so they are a body plus a free
Heartwood on curve. Pompous Battlemage is a one-mana prowess threat with a free loot. Codie is the force multiplier:
each prepared spell you cast is copied, so one free Vicious Verse drains twice and one free Soul Tether makes two
Heartwood tokens.

# Approach

## Game plan phases

| Phase | Turns | What you are doing |
|---|---|---|
| Setup | 1–2 | Heartwood Crafter on one, Konstrari Improviser or Stingerquill Voxmancer on two; cast the free back-face spell the turn the body lands |
| Build | 3–4 | Woodwork Prodigy and a noncreature-cast payoff: Firebrand Archer, Firespitter Whelp or Chandra's Emberling |
| Conversion | 5–6 | Codie plus two prepared bodies; every upkeep now produces two free spells and every copy triggers the whole payoff team |
| Close | 6+ | Prowess alpha strike with Hexhaven Dueling Arena re-arming an attacker, or drain the last points with Vicious Verse copies |

## Card roles

| Role | Cards | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Repeatable prepared engine | Woodwork Prodigy, Stingerquill Voxmancer | 8 | Both re-prepare in your upkeep, so each is a free spell every turn from the turn it lands |
| One-shot prepared bodies | Heartwood Crafter, Konstrari Improviser, Pompous Battlemage, Pyre Rhymer | 12 | Enter prepared: a body plus one free spell, and each back face is real value |
| Force multiplier | Codie, Ravenous Codex | 2 | Copies every prepared spell you cast; `{W}{U}{B}{R}{G}, {T}` makes each creature prepared at once |
| Noncreature payoffs | Firebrand Archer, Firespitter Whelp, Chandra's Emberling | 7 | 1 damage to each opponent per copy, or a +1/+1 counter per copy |
| Prowess threats | Pompous Battlemage, Pyre Rhymer, Grim Repriser | 8 | They grow off the same free spells the payoffs are counting |
| Recursion | Grim Repriser | 3 | `{B}{R}` brings it back with a finality counter, but only if an opponent took noncombat damage this turn — the ping team turns that on for free |
| Bodies and trample | Heartstring Puller | 2 | 3/1 trampler that leaves a 2/2 Cadet behind, which is the board you alpha strike with |

## Lands as engines

| Land | Count | What it does for the deck |
|---|---|---|
| Hexhaven Dueling Arena | 2 | `{2}, {T}`: target creature that attacked this turn becomes prepared, sorcery speed. Attack first, then re-arm for a second free spell in the same turn. `{4}, {T}` re-arms any creature, no attack needed |
| Mountain | 12 | The primary colour: Pyre Rhymer needs double red, and Molten Tide converts Mountain taps into extra mana |
| Forest | 7 | Casts Heartwood Crafter on one and pays the green half of every `{R/G}` hybrid |
| Swamp | 5 | Casts Grim Repriser and pays the black half of Stingerquill Voxmancer's hybrid |

Hexhaven Dueling Arena taps for `{C}`, so it never casts a coloured spell. Treat both copies as spells you cast on
turn five and later, not as mana sources.

## Curve and mana

| Mana value | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cards | 11 | 9 | 12 | 2 |

Twenty-six lands, eleven one-drops and nine two-drops: the deck has a prepared body on turn one in most games, which is
what holds goldfish turn-four consistency at 0.73 and P(four lands by turn four) at 0.737. Hybrid symbols (`{R/G}`,
`{B/R}`) mean almost every land casts almost every spell, which is why 24 basics are enough for three colours.

# Gameplay strategy

## Early game

Lead with a prepared body, not with a payoff. Heartwood Crafter on one is the ideal curve: it enters prepared, so turn
one is a 1/1 plus a free Soul Tether and a Heartwood token, and every later Soul Tether copy is another mana rock. Its
own `{T}: Add {C}` cannot pay for spells cast from your hand, so treat that ability as a bonus rather than a plan.

Stingerquill Voxmancer on one is the best turn-one play when you expect a long game — it is the cheapest repeatable
engine piece in the deck. Konstrari Improviser on two is the stronger clock: a 2/2 plus a Heartwood. Do not trade
Heartwood tokens for damage; they are the mana that casts Codie and Pyre Rhymer, and each one is also an artifact body
that survives a sweeper.

## The combo turn

The engine turn is not a single explosive loop — it is a repeating sequence you set up and then repeat every upkeep.

1. Have Woodwork Prodigy and Codie, Ravenous Codex on the battlefield by turn five.
2. In your upkeep, Woodwork Prodigy becomes prepared. Cast the Soul Tether copy. Codie copies it: two Heartwood tokens,
   two mana rocks, zero mana spent.
3. Cast anything else with a back face that is still prepared (Konstrari Improviser, Heartwood Crafter, Pyre Rhymer).
   Each cast is copied by Codie, and each cast triggers prowess, Firebrand Archer, Firespitter Whelp and Chandra's
   Emberling.
4. Attack. After attackers are declared, pay `{2}` and tap Hexhaven Dueling Arena to make the best attacker prepared
   again, then cast that back face in your second main phase for one more round of triggers.
5. With Stingerquill Voxmancer also on the board, the same upkeep produced a free Vicious Verse, which already turned on
   Grim Repriser's recursion clause for the turn.

The damage adds up from three directions at once: Vicious Verse copies hit for 1 each (2 with Codie), the ping payoffs
add 1 per opponent per copy, and every prowess attacker is 1/1 to 3/1 larger than printed by the time combat starts.

## Win condition 2 — Codie's mass preparation

Codie's second ability, `{W}{U}{B}{R}{G}, {T}`, makes each creature you control prepared. Because every creature in
this list has a back face, that is a board-wide free-spell turn: cast each back face, each one copied by Codie, each
one triggering the entire payoff team. Two prepared bodies and a ping team is usually eight to twelve points of
noncombat damage plus a lethal prowess swing. Save it for the turn you can also attack, since the copies are sorceries
and instants you cast in the second main phase.

Against a stalled board, the same turn is often just Pyre Rhymer's Molten Tide: for `{R}` every Mountain you tap adds
an extra `{R}`, which pays for a second and third prepared spell in the same turn.

## Mulligan guide

| Hand | Keep? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Two lands, Heartwood Crafter, Stingerquill Voxmancer | Yes | Both halves of the engine on curve, and the free spells start immediately |
| Three lands, Woodwork Prodigy, Firebrand Archer | Yes | The repeatable engine plus the payoff that turns it into damage |
| One land, two one-drops, no two-drop | Yes on the play | Eleven one-drops make this functional; on the draw it is a mulligan |
| Codie plus two ping payoffs, no prepared creature | No | Codie copies nothing without prepared spells to cast |
| Five lands, Grim Repriser, Firespitter Whelp | No | No engine, and Grim Repriser cannot return without noncombat damage |

## Key interactions and edge cases

- **Prepared is one-shot per preparation.** Casting the back-face copy unprepares the creature. Only Woodwork Prodigy
  and Stingerquill Voxmancer re-arm themselves, and only in your upkeep — so removal pointed at them costs you every
  future free spell, not just a body.
- **Codie copies, it does not cast.** The copy happens without being cast, so it does not trigger Firebrand Archer or
  prowess a second time. The value is the duplicated effect, not duplicated triggers.
- **Hexhaven Dueling Arena is sorcery speed on its `{2}` mode.** You must activate it in your second main phase after
  attackers are declared; the `{4}` mode has no attack requirement, which is how you re-arm a blocker.
- **Grim Repriser needs noncombat damage.** Vicious Verse copies, Firebrand Archer and Firespitter Whelp all satisfy it.
  In a turn where none of them resolved, the graveyard ability is switched off.
- **Molten Tide only counts Mountains.** It is a one-turn ritual for `{R}` per Mountain tap, not a permanent effect.
- **Codie is a 1/4 artifact creature.** It blocks well but dies to any two-power attacker.
- **A copy of a sorcery still obeys timing.** Sorcery back faces are main-phase only, so engine turns are sequenced
  around combat.

## Matchups

| Opponent | Plan |
|---|---|
| Aggro | Block with Codie and Heartstring Puller's Cadet, race with Firebrand Archer plus Vicious Verse copies. The deck's noncombat damage ignores their blockers |
| Control | Hold Woodwork Prodigy until they tap out on their turn, and keep a second engine piece in hand. Codie's mass-preparation turn is the one they must counter |
| Midrange | Grind with Grim Repriser recursion; their one-for-one removal cannot keep up with two engines |
| Combo | No countermagic, so the plan is speed: turn-one prepared body, turn-three payoff, and Vicious Verse copies to close the last points |
